# N-008 — Validation Matrix for 1080p60 / 1440p60 / 4K60 (T-009)

**Date:** 2026-05-13
**Scope:** v2.0.0 validation matrix and scripted test plan. Locks test rows, severity tiers, hardware/environment matrix, synthetic loads, pass/fail thresholds, evidence requirements, v1.1.0 regression coverage, Issues #1/#3/#4 absorption proofs, smoke suite, release-candidate suite, and the release-gate checklist that T-010 consumes.
**Status:** Design only. No test files, no CI, no helper or Electron code, no benchmark execution. This ticket defines the acceptance plan; it does not run benchmarks.

---

## 1. What the matrix has to prove

Three things, in order:

1. **v2 clears the v1.1.0 MediaRecorder ceiling.** On capable hardware (NVENC, VAAPI, QSV), 1440p60 and 4K60 must be reachable end-to-end (capture → encode → segment → export) without the upstream frame drops that the Chromium/Electron getDisplayMedia + canvas + MediaRecorder pipeline imposes. 1080p60 must remain stable.
2. **v2 does not regress the v1.1.0 fixes.** Replay corruption, fake duplicated-frame 60fps, save freeze during save, broken Linux hardware encoder fallback loops, audio sidecar stability, replay save state, replay source diagnostics, FPS/cadence detection, process cleanup — each has a named regression row.
3. **v2 absorbs Issues #1, #3, #4 structurally.** Each issue has at least one row that asserts the new structural property (region as a first-class capture mode; `capture.sessionReady` as the only entry to RECORDING; three separate clocks with no shared state). The rows fail loudly if the structural property is violated, not if a cosmetic UI detail drifts.

Implementation is out of scope. This note is the contract. T-010 consumes it as the release-gate checklist.

---

## 2. Severity tiers

| tier | meaning | failure blocks release? |
|---|---|---|
| `must-pass` | required for v2.0.0 GA | **yes** |
| `smoke` | subset of must-pass that completes in ≤ 30 min on a single workstation; runs on every branch | yes (smoke red ⇒ branch not RC-ready) |
| `rc` | full release-candidate run across encoder paths × target resolutions; includes soak | yes |
| `regression` | v1.1.0 fix carry-forward; pre-defined failure mode | yes |
| `soak` | long-duration (≥ 15 min); some must-pass, some nice-to-have | per row |
| `nice-to-have` | non-blocking | no |

`smoke ⊂ must-pass ⊂ rc`. `regression ⊂ must-pass`. `soak` is orthogonal — a soak row can be must-pass or nice-to-have.

A row is **scripted-local** if a single repo-local script (no special CI hardware) can drive and assert it once the helper has CLI handles. A row is **manual** if a human has to drive the portal pick, observe overlay UX, or read a HUD. A row is **future-CI** if it requires hardware not in the smoke workstation; it is still must-pass for RC, just executed on the RC matrix.

---

## 3. Row format

Every row carries: `id`, `title`, `tier`, `type` (manual / scripted-local / future-CI), `hw`, `resolution`, `encoder`, `pre`, `procedure`, `pass`, `fail`, `evidence`, `owner_on_fail`, `linked_source_case`. The matrix below uses compact markdown tables; the final scripted-test corpus (one JSON per row) is left to T-010 and onward. This note locks the row set, the pass/fail thresholds, and the evidence requirements.

`owner_on_fail` is one of: **capture** (N-003), **encoder** (N-004), **segment** (N-005), **export** (N-006), **ui** (renderer FSM/UX, N-007), **supervision** (helper lifecycle, N-007 §6), **packaging** (deps/sha256/install). A row with a single owner is preferable; rows with multiple owners are split if possible.

---

## 4. Hardware / environment matrix

The matrix below is the **RC machine set**. Smoke runs only on row M1. Manual rows on M5 require human interaction; everything else is intended to be drivable by a repo-local script.

| id | OS | compositor / DE | GPU vendor | encoder paths exercised | role |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **M1** | Arch / Wayland | KDE Plasma 6 | NVIDIA RTX 40-class | NVENC, libx264 | **smoke workstation**, primary dev |
| **M2** | Ubuntu LTS / Wayland | GNOME 46+ | AMD RDNA3 (e.g. 7800 XT) | VAAPI, libx264 | AMD primary |
| **M3** | Fedora / Wayland | KDE Plasma 6 | Intel Arc A-series | QSV (preferred), VAAPI (fallback), libx264 | Intel/Arc |
| **M4** | Debian stable / Wayland | wlroots (Sway) | Intel iGPU (UHD class) | QSV, VAAPI, libx264 | older Intel, wlroots backend |
| **M5** | Arch / Wayland | KDE Plasma 6 | NVIDIA (same class as M1) | NVENC, libx264 | **manual UX** machine |
| **W1** | Windows 11 | DWM | NVIDIA | (future) WGC capture + NVENC | placeholder only; v2.0.0 documents "AMF future slot, falls through visibly" |

Smoke = M1 only. RC = M1+M2+M3+M4 mandatory; M5 for manual rows; W1 only for documentation (no Windows release in v2.0.0).

Environment preconditions verified by `coveApi.env.probe()` per N-007 §15 (xdg-desktop-portal ≥ 1.18, pipewire ≥ 0.3.x, libx264 present, helper sha256 matches, GPU driver query succeeds). A machine that fails the probe does not enter the matrix until fixed; that is itself **VAL-PKG-001**.

---

## 5. Synthetic load definitions

Real desktop content is uncontrolled. Synthetic loads make pass/fail deterministic.

| load id | description | what it stresses | source |
|---|---|---|---|
| **L-MOTION-60** | full-screen smooth horizontal scroll, 60 fps frame-perfect, embedded frame counter (PTS encoded in pixels) | encoder steady-state, cadence preservation, duplicate-frame detection | fullscreen test page or compiled GL widget; repo provides asset spec only |
| **L-STATIC** | static desktop, single small blinking 1Hz indicator | idle path, GOP keyframe correctness | any |
| **L-CHANGE** | 5 s static → 5 s motion → 5 s static, repeated | dynamic bitrate, segment boundary stability | scripted compositor switch or window animation |
| **L-RESIZE** | source window resized once mid-capture | `capture.formatChanged` handling (N-003 §10) | manual |
| **L-MINIMIZE** | source window minimised or fully covered for 60 s | Issue #3 absorption — no hover dependency | manual |
| **L-PORTAL-DENY** | user clicks Cancel on the portal dialog | `portal-denied` reason code | manual |
| **L-SOURCE-REMOVE** | source window closed mid-capture | `source-removed` reason code, FSM `SESSION_LOST` | manual or scripted via wmctrl |
| **L-COMP-PAUSE** | screensaver or compositor blank engages mid-capture | DMA-BUF/SHM transitions, pause/resume events | manual |
| **L-DISK-SLOW** | segment dir on a `dm-delay`-throttled mount (50 MB/s ceiling) | slow-disk path in N-005 §10 | scripted-local |
| **L-DISK-FULL** | segment dir on a 200 MiB tmpfs that fills | `segment-sink-disk-full`, FSM `SESSION_LOST` | scripted-local |
| **L-CRASH-CAP** | `SIGKILL` the helper mid-capture | crash detection, restart loop, recovery banner | scripted-local |
| **L-CRASH-EXP** | `SIGKILL` the helper mid-export | export orphan reaping, snapshot release | scripted-local |
| **L-AUDIO-SYNC** | audio synthesizer emitting 1 kHz tick every second, encoded into the video as a flash | A/V sync within tolerance (when audio lands; placeholder must-pass row when audio lands) | future-audio asset |

The repo does not need to ship the asset binaries; the spec (PTS-in-pixels format, frame counter encoding, tick cadence) is what T-009 fixes. Asset creation is a T-010 implementation task.

---

## 6. Universal pass/fail thresholds

These apply across the matrix unless a row narrows them.

### 6.1 Frame integrity

- **Capture drop rate (capable HW).** Over a 60 s capture at the target resolution/fps with the synthetic load `L-MOTION-60`, the helper's `capture.diagnostics.framesDropped` SHALL be **0** at 1080p60 and 1440p60 on NVENC/VAAPI/QSV; ≤ **0.1 %** at 4K60 on NVENC/VAAPI; ≤ **0.5 %** at 4K60 on QSV; ≤ **2 %** at 4K60 on libx264 (acceptable degraded path; surfaced via `encoder.backPressure`, not silent).
- **Encoder drop rate (capable HW).** `encoder.diagnostics.framesDroppedAtEncoder` SHALL be **0** for 1080p/1440p on any HW encoder; ≤ **0.1 %** at 4K60 on NVENC/VAAPI; libx264 4K60 may legitimately be encoder-bound — that case must engage `encoder.backPressure`, never silently drop.
- **No fake duplicated frames.** Output MP4 SHALL contain `round(duration_s × declared_fps) ± 1` decoded frames. Duplicated-PTS pairs ≤ 1 per 60 s. `ffprobe -show_frames -select_streams v` SHALL NOT show consecutive frames with identical pkt_dts within ½ frame duration. This is the load-bearing v1.1.0 regression check.
- **Cadence.** Mean inter-frame PTS interval within **±0.5 %** of the nominal (16.6̄ ms at 60 fps). 95th percentile within **±2 %**. 99th percentile within **±5 %**.

### 6.2 Duration

- Output duration SHALL match the requested replay window within **±1 frame** for 30 s and 60 s windows, **±50 ms** for 5 min, **±200 ms** for 10 min, **±500 ms** for soak windows ≥ 15 min. Tolerance grows with cumulative clock error, not encoder error.
- "Output duration" = `ffprobe -show_format -of csv=p=0 -i out.mp4` `duration` field; **also** verify by counting decoded frames against declared fps, to catch the v1.1.0 fake-60fps class.

### 6.3 Save latency / non-freeze

- `replay.save` SHALL return a `ReplaySnapshot` within **≤ 250 ms + the current fragment's remaining encode time** (worst case ≈ 250 ms + 2 s GOP = 2.25 s). Measured at the IPC boundary in the helper, surfaced as `replay.diagnostics.saveLatencyMs`.
- During SAVING, the renderer HUD timer SHALL continue updating at **≥ 1 Hz**. Measured by collecting timestamps of the renderer's `capture.diagnostics` event arrivals during the SAVING window; ≥ 1 sample per second must be observed. **No HUD freeze.**
- Active capture frame production SHALL continue during SAVING with no observed drop spike (drop rate during the save window within 2× the 60 s pre-save baseline).

### 6.4 Export concurrency

- Capture frame production SHALL continue during EXPORTING with the same drop tolerance as 6.3.
- Each export SHALL emit **exactly one terminal event** (`export.completed | export.failed | export.cancelled | export.rejected`) per `exportId`. Counted by a scripted-local subscriber.

### 6.5 Encoder fallback

- Hardware encoder runtime failure SHALL emit `encoder.fallbackEngaged` **at most once per session** (no mid-session re-switching — N-004 §15). On Linux finalization, re-encode SHALL use **libx264 only** (N-004 §10).
- Negative encoder probe SHALL be cached in the persisted probe cache and SHALL NOT be re-tried within the cache TTL (per N-004 §6). Manual reset only.
- `encoder.selected` SHALL be visible in `engine.diagnosticsBundle` and in `Settings → Diagnostics`. `encoder.fallbackEngaged` SHALL show in the HUD as a non-intrusive indicator.

### 6.6 Process cleanup

- 5 seconds after `engine.shutdown` (or process quit), `pgrep -u $UID '(cove-replay-engine|ffmpeg|pactl)'` SHALL return **zero rows**. This row is run after every must-pass capture/export row, not as a one-off — leftover-process regression is the v1.1.0 carry-forward.
- The socket `engine.sock` and pid file `engine.pid` SHALL be absent.
- `pactl` SHALL never appear in the matrix output. The v2 helper does not use `pactl`; presence of a `pactl` child is an automatic packaging/supervision failure.

### 6.7 Recovery

- After `L-CRASH-CAP`, next helper boot SHALL surface a `replay.recoveryAvailable` for the killed session within **≤ 2 s** of helper ready. Partial (uncommitted) segments SHALL be absent from the recovered manifest. Committed segments (those with finalized mfra/sidx) SHALL be present.
- After `L-CRASH-EXP`, next helper boot SHALL scan `exports/manifest.jsonl` and unlink orphans (N-006 §15) before opening the IPC socket. `engine.ready` arrives only after orphan reap completes.

### 6.8 Supervision

- Restart loop bounded: ≤ **3** restarts in **60 s**, then sticky `engine.unavailable`. Counter visible in `main.log`.
- Helper sha256 mismatch SHALL refuse boot with `helper-binary-tampered`. Renderer SHALL show a blocking modal (N-007 §17.1). Recovery action = reinstall.
- Helper protocol mismatch SHALL refuse boot with `helper-protocol-mismatch`. Renderer SHALL show a blocking modal.

### 6.9 Audio (when audio lands)

- Placeholder rows are listed; `must-pass` for v2.0.0-with-audio, not for v2.0.0 video-only GA.
- A/V drift ≤ **40 ms** over 60 s; ≤ **80 ms** over 5 min; ≤ **200 ms** over soak. Measured against `L-AUDIO-SYNC` tick→flash alignment in the final MP4.
- No leftover `pactl` (v2 does not use it — see 6.6). Audio path uses PipeWire API directly.

---

## 7. Required diagnostics / evidence (collected per row)

Each row, when failing or as a sanity baseline when passing, saves the following bundle. The bundle is what makes "did the test pass" answerable a week later from a different machine.

| artifact | source | purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `engine.diagnosticsBundle.zip` | helper `engine.copyDiagnosticsBundle()` (N-007 §16) | last N per-session JSON dumps + helper log tail + main log tail + redacted settings + env manifest |
| `capture.json` | helper per-session dump (N-003 §14) | sessionReady ts, formats negotiated, framesProduced, framesDropped, formatChanged events, source descriptor |
| `encoder.json` | helper per-session dump (N-004 §17) | selected backend, probe result, fallbackEngaged events, runtime errors, framesEncoded, framesDroppedAtEncoder, backPressure events |
| `segments.json` | helper per-session dump (N-005 §14) | committed segments (path, duration, byteSize, ptsStart, ptsEnd), evicted segments, pinned segments, disk-full events |
| `export.json` per `exportId` | helper per-export dump (N-006 §16) | stage timeline, progress samples, terminal event, exitCode if ffmpeg, reason if failed/cancelled, durationMs |
| `out.mp4` | export output | direct artefact under test |
| `out.mp4.ffprobe.json` | scripted-local `ffprobe -of json -show_format -show_streams -show_packets -show_frames` (frames truncated to first N for size) | duration, fps, codec, frame count, PTS sequence |
| `out.mp4.mediainfo.json` | scripted-local `mediainfo --Output=JSON` | bitrate, GOP, fragment structure cross-check |
| `pre_pgrep.txt` / `post_pgrep.txt` | scripted-local `pgrep -au $UID` before and 5 s after shutdown | process cleanup invariant |
| `renderer-events.jsonl` | scripted-local IPC sniffer / renderer test harness | sequence of FSM events, HUD timer samples during SAVING |
| `dmesg.tail` | scripted-local `journalctl --since "<run start>"` | kernel-level GPU / portal / DRM errors |

Evidence is uploaded by the runner (T-010) to a per-run directory; the matrix specifies what; T-010 specifies where.

Sensitive content rule: diagnostics bundles are redacted of file paths above the recording (per N-007 §16); the redaction is itself **VAL-DIAG-002**.

---

## 8. Capture validation matrix (VAL-CAP)

Source design: N-003 §17 (cases 1–28). Each row below references its upstream case.

| id | title | tier | type | hw | res | encoder | pass | owner_on_fail | linked |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| VAL-CAP-001 | PipeWire portal `sessionReady` arrives within 5 s of accept | smoke / must-pass | manual | any | 1080p60 | NVENC | event observed; tsNs monotonic; HUD does not start until event | capture | N-003 §5 |
| VAL-CAP-002 | Quick-pick via stored restore token skips portal dialog | must-pass | manual | any | 1080p60 | any | no portal dialog shown; `capture.sessionReady` emitted | capture | N-003 §5 |
| VAL-CAP-003 | Portal denial → `portal-denied` → FSM PICKING again | smoke / must-pass | manual | any | N/A | n/a | reason emitted; renderer returns to PICKING; no helper restart | capture | N-003 §5 |
| VAL-CAP-004 | Monitor capture 60 s `L-MOTION-60` produces declared frame count | smoke / must-pass | scripted-local | M1 | 1080p60 | NVENC | drop ≤ 0; cadence per 6.1; frame counter monotonic | capture | N-003 §17 c.1 |
| VAL-CAP-005 | Window capture 60 s on a focused source | must-pass | manual | M1 | 1080p60 | NVENC | as VAL-CAP-004 | capture | N-003 §17 c.2 |
| VAL-CAP-006 | **Minimised source 60 s — no hover dependency (Issue #3 proof)** | must-pass / regression | manual | M1 | 1080p60 | NVENC | declared frame count produced even while source window is minimised or behind another window for the full 60 s; HUD timer increments | capture | N-003 §17 c.24 |
| VAL-CAP-007 | Region capture; rectangle changed mid-recording (Issue #1 proof) | must-pass | manual | M1 | 1080p60 (region) | NVENC | `capture.setRegion` hot-applies; helper crops at encoder boundary; no session restart; output cropped correctly | capture / ui | N-003 §6 |
| VAL-CAP-008 | `L-RESIZE` mid-capture → `capture.formatChanged` handled | must-pass | manual | M1 | 1080p60 → 1440p60 | NVENC | one `formatChanged` event; segment boundary lands at the change; no dropped frames at the transition beyond 6.1 | capture | N-003 §10 |
| VAL-CAP-009 | DMA-BUF path selected when available | must-pass | scripted-local | M1, M2, M3 | 1080p60 | any HW | `capture.diagnostics.bufferType === "dmabuf"`; encoder zero-copy import succeeds | capture | N-003 §9 |
| VAL-CAP-010 | SHM fallback when DMA-BUF rejected | must-pass | scripted-local | any | 1080p60 | any HW | `bufferType === "shm"`; no helper restart; one entry in encoder.diagnostics noting fallback | capture | N-003 §9 |
| VAL-CAP-011 | `L-SOURCE-REMOVE` mid-capture | must-pass | manual | any | 1080p60 | any | `source-removed` reason; renderer FSM → SESSION_LOST (sticky); no helper crash | capture / ui | N-003 §5 |
| VAL-CAP-012 | `L-COMP-PAUSE` (screensaver) mid-capture | must-pass | manual | any | 1080p60 | any | `streamPaused` and `streamResumed` events; no drops attributed to compositor pause; HUD shows paused state | capture / ui | N-003 §10 |
| VAL-CAP-013 | 1440p60 monitor capture 60 s on each HW path | rc / must-pass | scripted-local | M1 (NVENC), M2 (VAAPI), M3 (QSV) | 1440p60 | NVENC / VAAPI / QSV | per 6.1 | capture / encoder | N-003 §17 c.1 |
| VAL-CAP-014 | 4K60 monitor capture 60 s on each HW path | rc / must-pass | scripted-local | M1 (NVENC), M2 (VAAPI), M3 (QSV) | 4K60 | NVENC / VAAPI / QSV | per 6.1 (4K thresholds) | capture / encoder | N-003 §17 c.1 |
| VAL-CAP-015 | 4K60 monitor capture 60 s on libx264 (CPU) | rc / nice-to-have | scripted-local | M1 with HW disabled | 4K60 | libx264 | drop ≤ 2 %; `encoder.backPressure` observed if encoder-bound; no silent loss | encoder | N-003 §17 c.1 |

Soak rows from VAL-CAP:

| id | title | tier | duration |
|---|---|---|---|
| VAL-CAP-S1 | 15-min replay buffer 1080p60 on each HW path | rc / must-pass / soak | 15 min |
| VAL-CAP-S2 | 60-min replay buffer 1080p60 | rc / nice-to-have / soak | 60 min |
| VAL-CAP-S3 | 15-min replay buffer 1440p60 | rc / must-pass / soak | 15 min |
| VAL-CAP-S4 | 15-min replay buffer 4K60 (NVENC + VAAPI) | rc / must-pass / soak | 15 min |

> **VAL-CAP-006 adjudication note (T-027):** VAL-CAP-006 is split for adjudication into **VAL-CAP-006a** (minimised/occluded source survival — Issue #3 proof; existing §16/§17/§22 references resolve here) and **VAL-CAP-006b** (declared frame-count tolerance under zero-copy DMA-BUF). See §26. The row above and its §6.1 thresholds are unchanged.

## 9. Encoder validation matrix (VAL-ENC)

Source design: N-004 §20 (cases 1–18).

| id | title | tier | type | encoder | pass | owner |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| VAL-ENC-001 | Positive probe — NVENC | smoke / must-pass | scripted-local | NVENC | `encoder.probeResult.ok === true`; `encoder.selected.backend === "nvenc"`; persisted to probe cache | encoder |

| VAL-ENC-003 | Positive probe — QSV on Intel/Arc | rc / must-pass | scripted-local | QSV | `selected.backend === "qsv"` | encoder |
| VAL-ENC-004 | Negative probe — NVENC simulated failure | must-pass | scripted-local | n/a | `probeResult.ok === false`; cached; next launch does not re-probe within TTL; `fallbackEngaged` to libx264 (live) on Linux only when no other HW path is left | encoder |
| VAL-ENC-005 | Manual probe cache reset | must-pass | manual | any | `Settings → Reset encoder probe` clears cache; next session re-probes; new selection takes effect for next session only (no mid-session switch) | encoder / ui |
| VAL-ENC-006 | Selected backend visible in UI | smoke / must-pass | manual | any | `Settings → Diagnostics` shows current `encoder.selected`; HUD shows compact badge | encoder / ui |
| VAL-ENC-007 | Fallback indicator visible | must-pass | manual | any | After `fallbackEngaged`, HUD shows a non-intrusive indicator; not silent | encoder / ui |
| VAL-ENC-008 | **No mid-session encoder switching** | must-pass | scripted-local | any | Induce a runtime encoder error 30 s into capture; helper does NOT switch backends mid-session; emits `encoder.runtimeError`; session ends cleanly; next session may pick a different backend per cache | encoder |
| VAL-ENC-009 | libx264 universal fallback | must-pass | scripted-local | libx264 | All HW backends artificially disabled (env override); helper still captures and produces a valid MP4 at 1080p60 | encoder |

| VAL-ENC-011 | **No blind hardware encoder retry loops** (Issue carry-forward) | must-pass / regression | scripted-local | any | Induce repeated runtime HW failures; helper emits `runtimeError` and ends; **no exponential or unbounded retry** of the same HW path within a session; new sessions consult the cached negative result | encoder |
| VAL-ENC-012 | AMF future slot is visibly inert in v2.0.0 | must-pass | scripted-local | n/a | On Linux, requesting `encoder.preference === "amf"` falls through with a `fallbackEngaged` of reason `amf-unavailable-on-linux`; never silent | encoder |
| VAL-ENC-013 | `encoder.backPressure` surfaced under 4K60 libx264 | must-pass | scripted-local | libx264 | `L-MOTION-60` 4K60 on CPU-only path emits `backPressure` events before any drop; HUD shows the indicator | encoder |

## 10. Rolling buffer validation matrix (VAL-SEG)

Source design: N-005 §19. Default GOP ≈ 2 s; default fMP4 segment = 1 GOP.

| id | title | tier | type | pass | owner |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| VAL-SEG-001 | 30 s / 60 s / 2 min / 5 min / 10 min replay window — bounded disk growth | smoke (60 s row only) / must-pass | scripted-local | total committed-segment byte sum stays within `±10 %` of `bitrate × window` after the window fills; older segments evicted | segment |
| VAL-SEG-002 | Atomic segment commit | must-pass | scripted-local | each committed segment file passes `ffprobe` integrity check; no partial files appear in the committed index | segment |
| VAL-SEG-003 | `replay.save` while capture continues | smoke / must-pass | scripted-local | save latency per 6.3; capture drop tolerance per 6.3; segments produced during save are committed normally | segment |
| VAL-SEG-004 | Pin defers eviction | must-pass | scripted-local | open a snapshot via `replay.save`, hold for 30 s past the rolling window edge; the underlying segments are not evicted; after `replay.snapshot_release`, eviction proceeds | segment |
| VAL-SEG-005 | `L-DISK-SLOW` 50 MB/s ceiling at 1080p60 | rc / must-pass | scripted-local | helper either keeps up (preferred) or surfaces `segment-sink-back-pressure`; never silently loses committed segments; FSM does not lie | segment |
| VAL-SEG-006 | `L-DISK-FULL` mid-capture | rc / must-pass | scripted-local | `segment-sink-disk-full` reason; FSM → SESSION_LOST sticky; helper does not crash; recoverable session offered next boot for the committed-up-to-failure window | segment / ui |
| VAL-SEG-007 | **Crash recovery: committed segments recovered, partial segment discarded** | must-pass / regression | scripted-local | `L-CRASH-CAP` mid-segment; next boot's `replay.recoveryAvailable` lists committed segments only; the in-flight partial file is absent or quarantined; no partial file shows up in the recovered timeline | segment |
| VAL-SEG-008 | Snapshot is paths, not bytes | must-pass | scripted-local | `ReplaySnapshot` returned from `replay.save` contains segment paths, not byte buffers; helper memory does not spike by `bitrate × window` on save | segment |
| VAL-SEG-009 | Replay window change while running | nice-to-have | manual | settings change is queued; existing run continues with old window; new window takes effect on next session | segment / ui |

## 11. Export / remux validation matrix (VAL-EXP)

Source design: N-006 §18. State machine: `PREPARING → REMUXING|REENCODING → MUXING → FINALIZING → done`; `Cancel` disabled past MUXING.

| id | title | tier | type | pass | owner |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| VAL-EXP-001 | Fast stream-copy path | smoke / must-pass | scripted-local | export of a snapshot whose segments are codec-compatible runs `REMUXING`-only, no re-encode; final MP4 has identical packet PTS to the source segments; duration per 6.2; **no fake duplicated frames** | export |
| VAL-EXP-002 | Lead trim re-encode | must-pass | scripted-local | snapshot whose head is mid-GOP; export re-encodes only the lead GOP via libx264; remainder stream-copies; final duration per 6.2 | export |
| VAL-EXP-003 | Discontinuity re-encode | must-pass | scripted-local | snapshot spanning a `formatChanged` boundary; export re-encodes around the discontinuity; final duration per 6.2; **cadence preserved** (no fake-60fps repair) | export |
| VAL-EXP-004 | Maximum compatibility full re-encode | rc / must-pass | scripted-local | `maxCompatibility: true` forces full re-encode via libx264; final MP4 plays in QuickTime, Windows Media Player, Firefox | export |
| VAL-EXP-005 | Cancel before MUXING | must-pass | scripted-local | cancel during REMUXING/REENCODING; emits `export.cancelled`; ffmpeg child reaped; no temp files remain | export |
| VAL-EXP-006 | Cancel disabled past MUXING | must-pass | scripted-local | UI Cancel disabled; sending `replay.export_cancel` past MUXING is rejected with a stable reason code; export still completes | export / ui |
| VAL-EXP-007 | Failure path: ffmpeg nonzero | must-pass | scripted-local | induced ffmpeg failure; emits `export.failed` with `ffmpeg-exited-nonzero`; row in renderer shows "Show diagnostics"; temp files cleaned | export |
| VAL-EXP-008 | **Exactly one terminal event per `exportId`** | must-pass / regression | scripted-local | over 100 induced exports (mix of success/cancel/fail), each `exportId` produces exactly one of `completed|failed|cancelled|rejected` | export |

## 20. ffprobe / mediainfo check recipes

These are the canonical numerical checks. Recipes are spec-level; T-010 wraps them in a runner.

- **Duration.** `ffprobe -v error -show_entries format=duration -of csv=p=0 "$f"` → compare to requested window per 6.2.
- **Declared fps.** `ffprobe -v error -select_streams v -show_entries stream=r_frame_rate -of csv=p=0 "$f"` (parse `num/den`).
- **Frame count.** `ffprobe -v error -select_streams v -count_packets -show_entries stream=nb_read_packets -of csv=p=0 "$f"` → compare to `round(duration × declared_fps)` per 6.1.
- **Duplicated PTS detection.** `ffprobe -v error -select_streams v -show_frames -of json "$f"` → walk `pkt_dts`/`best_effort_timestamp`; any run of consecutive identical timestamps within ½ frame duration counts as a violation. Allow 1 per 60 s. Used to prove VAL-EXP-010, VAL-REG-002.
- **Real cadence.** Same dump as above; compute mean and 95/99 percentile inter-frame interval; compare to nominal per 6.1.
- **Faststart.** `mediainfo --Output=JSON "$f" | jq -r '.media.track[0].IsStreamable'` (= `"Yes"`); cross-check by `ffprobe -v error -show_entries format=tags "$f"` and confirm `moov` precedes `mdat` via `python -c "import struct,sys; ..."` (T-010 specifies the exact one-liner).
- **Codec.** `ffprobe -v error -select_streams v -show_entries stream=codec_name -of csv=p=0 "$f"` → `h264` for v2.0.0 video paths; `hevc` only if the encoder selection picked it intentionally (out of scope for v2.0.0 GA — h264 only).
- **GOP / fragment structure.** `mediainfo --Output=JSON` → confirm fMP4 fragmenting on segment files; final MP4 may be non-fragmented after `FINALIZING` (mp4 with `faststart`).

## 26. Audit-safe disposition policy: cannot-validate and the VAL-CAP-006 split (T-027)

**Status:** Policy addition (T-027). Additive to this note. Changes no threshold, no §6.1 text, no row-driver behavior, no runner status union, and no automated verdict. It governs how manual rows are *adjudicated* and recorded, not how the runner computes counts. `verdictFromCounts` and the runner status union are unchanged; `cannot-validate` is a §24 adjudication disposition, never a runner verdict.

**Why this section exists.** ISS-011 showed that VAL-CAP-006's declared-frame-count criterion cannot be honestly adjudicated on the M1-class NVIDIA / KDE Plasma 6 / Wayland stack: DMA-BUF zero-copy negotiation hard-fails on that hardware, so only SHM-fallback evidence exists, and there is no working zero-copy baseline on the host to measure declared frame count against. Before this section the policy had only `pass`/`fail` plus skip; a precondition-unavailable row had no honest home, and a skip-only (or skip+pass) automated suite summary could read as gate-green. This section closes that gap without letting "cannot validate" become "pass."

### 26.1 Disposition taxonomy

Every adjudicated row resolves to exactly one of three audit dispositions:

- **pass** — the assertion was evaluated and met. Green. Satisfies §24.
- **fail** — the assertion was evaluated and not met. Red. Blocks per §24 and the §22 stop-on-first-red rule.
- **cannot-validate** — a complete, evidence-backed platform predicate (§26.4) proves the row's required precondition is unavailable on this host class, so the assertion could be *neither* evaluated to pass *nor* to fail. **Not green. Never satisfies §24.** The cell is parked pending validation on qualifying cross-platform hardware.

This taxonomy does **not** add a formal `blocked` disposition; N-008 wording does not require one, and T-027 is deliberately scoped to `cannot-validate` only. (Operational blocking of a *ticket* remains a storybloq workflow concern, separate from row adjudication.)

### 26.2 Definition of cannot-validate

A row may be adjudicated `cannot-validate` only when **all** of the following hold:

- a complete, evidence-backed platform predicate (§26.4) proves the row's required precondition is **unavailable** on this host class;
- the assertion was therefore **not** passed;
- the assertion was therefore **not** failed;
- the cell is **never** rendered green and **never** counted toward §24 satisfaction;
- the cell is parked pending cross-platform validation on hardware where the precondition *is* available.

`cannot-validate` is an honest "we could not put this assertion to the test on this host," not a soft pass. It carries no credit and never becomes `pass` or `skip`.

### 26.3 Anti-abuse rule (cannot-validate is strictly narrower than fail)

`cannot-validate` eligibility is **strictly narrower** than `fail` eligibility. A row qualifies for `cannot-validate` only when the platform predicate (§26.4) is *complete and unambiguous*. If the platform predicate is **incomplete, ambiguous, partially satisfied, or the host class is unsupported/unknown**, the row does **not** qualify for `cannot-validate` and **falls back to normal adjudication** (pass/fail) under the existing thresholds. On any doubt the default is ordinary adjudication, never `cannot-validate`. This prevents `cannot-validate` from becoming an escape hatch that launders a real defect into a non-red state.

### 26.4 Platform predicate (deterministic, evidence-backed)

`cannot-validate` for a zero-copy-dependent row is eligible **only when every one of these required artifacts is present** for the capture session under adjudication:

1. **GPU vendor:** `gpuInfo` (capture/encoder diagnostics) starts with `"nvidia:"`.
2. **Compositor / session:** Wayland + KDE (Plasma) evidence is present (session type Wayland; KDE/Plasma desktop).
3. **Zero-copy unavailability:** the helper log for that capture session shows **DMA-BUF negotiation failure** followed by **SHM fallback** for the session (i.e., zero-copy was attempted, hard-failed, and capture proceeded on SHM).

All three are required and must be drawn from session evidence, not prose assertion. Missing or ambiguous on any one ⇒ predicate incomplete ⇒ §26.3 fallback to normal adjudication. The predicate is what distinguishes a **product defect** (capture/encoder cannot hold cadence on a working path) from an **environment limitation** (the working zero-copy path does not exist on this host) — that distinction is determined by predicate evidence, never by narrative.

### 26.5 §24 guard — row-level adjudication beats suite-level aggregation (manual rows)

For manual rows, the suite-level *automated* verdict aggregation does **not** override the row-level adjudication recorded against this note's §24 release-gate checklist. Specifically: a skip-only, or skip+pass, automated suite summary **must not** be treated as gate-green. A `cannot-validate` row keeps its §24 checklist item **non-green** (parked), exactly as a `fail` keeps it red — it never silently rolls up into a green suite. The runner's counts and status union are unchanged; this is an adjudication/reporting rule layered on top of them, consistent with the §22 stop-on-first-red rule.

### 26.6 VAL-CAP-006 split

The §8 row **VAL-CAP-006** ("Minimised source 60 s — no hover dependency, Issue #3 proof") is split, for adjudication, into two cells. The §8 table row and its §6.1 thresholds are **unchanged**; this is a policy refinement of how that row is judged and where its evidence maps. The split mirrors ISS-011's two observed legs (leg 1 = declared frame count; leg 2 = HUD timer increments):

- **VAL-CAP-006a — minimised/occluded source survival.** Manual, must-pass, `owner_on_fail: capture`. Asserts that with the source window minimised or fully occluded for the full 60 s, capture **survives**, the **HUD timer continues to increment** (ISS-011 leg 2, which passed), and the export produces a **valid, playable output**. This is the Issue #3 structural proof (the source records while minimised — no hover dependency). **All existing references to VAL-CAP-006 — §16 VAL-REG-012, §17 (the Issue #3 absorption row), and §22 smoke item 5 — resolve to VAL-CAP-006a.** 006a does **not** depend on a zero-copy path and is adjudicated normally (pass/fail).
- **VAL-CAP-006b — declared frame-count tolerance under zero-copy.** Manual, must-pass on qualifying DMA-BUF platforms, `owner_on_fail: capture / encoder`. Asserts the §6.1 declared-frame-count tolerance (`round(duration_s × declared_fps) ± 1`; threshold **unchanged**) under a working **zero-copy (DMA-BUF)** capture path. This is ISS-011 leg 1, the leg that failed under SHM. 006b is the cell that ISS-011 could not adjudicate on M1.

### 26.7 ISS-011 evidence mapping

The historical ISS-011 evidence is mapped, by path and **without renaming or moving it**, to **VAL-CAP-006b**:

`.story/handovers/evidence/2026-05-22-t-010c-slice-3-m1-smoke-completion-retry-2/operator-evidence/VAL-CAP-006/`

(contains `BLOCKED.md`, `ffprobe-frame-count.txt`, `helper-log-excerpt.txt`, `hud-during-minimised.png`, `source-minimised.png`). That evidence documents the 1200 / 1671 declared-frame-count deficit (28%) observed under SHM fallback at 4K on the M1 NVIDIA / KDE Wayland host, with DMA-BUF hard-failing on both portal sessions.

### 26.8 NVIDIA/KDE SHM disposition for VAL-CAP-006b

On the M1-class NVIDIA / KDE Plasma 6 / Wayland host, where the §26.4 predicate is **complete** (`gpuInfo` starts `nvidia:`, Wayland+KDE present, DMA-BUF failure + SHM fallback in the session log), **VAL-CAP-006b is adjudicated `cannot-validate`**: the declared-frame-count deficit was observed only under SHM fallback, with no working zero-copy baseline on the host to put the assertion to the test. This is **not** a pass and does **not** green the §24 item; the cell is parked. **VAL-CAP-006b must produce a real pass/fail on AMD (VAAPI) or Intel (QSV) DMA-BUF hardware where zero-copy succeeds** — tracked by follow-up **T-028**. If, on such hardware with the zero-copy path confirmed working (`capture.diagnostics.bufferType === "dmabuf"`, per VAL-CAP-009), the declared-frame-count deficit persists beyond the §6.1 tolerance, that is a real capture/encoder defect (**fail**), not `cannot-validate`. VAL-CAP-006a is unaffected by this disposition and is adjudicated normally on every host.
